sovereign_country.strategic_role: 北美成熟市场、联邦与省两级公司实体设立（EPC合规）

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Wholesale International Distribution of Acetate Eyeglass Frames

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada has an extensive network of bilateral tax treaties; treaty entitlement and withholding-tax outcomes depend on the relevant counterparty country and the partner's tax residence.
Canada-United States-Mexico Agreement (CUSMA) applies to qualifying trade and investment, subject to its terms.
Canada's foreign investment protection agreements apply only where the relevant treaty is in force and the investor and investment satisfy its definitions.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Alberta limited partnerships are governed principally by the Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, and the Limited Partnerships Act, RSA 2000, c L-7, together with applicable regulations. Alberta has no generally applicable beneficial-ownership register for limited partnerships equivalent to the corporate transparency register applicable to Alberta corporations. The federal Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, and regulations impose AML duties on reporting entities, not generally on an ordinary wholesale limited partnership solely by reason of its formation. Partnership registration and filings are administered under Alberta registry legislation and procedures.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign limited partner's certificate of existence or equivalent entity-status evidence, if requested by the registry agent, bank, or counterparty
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company registry or other competent public authority in the partner's jurisdiction of formation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where the issuing state and document qualify; otherwise consular legalization, subject to recipient requirements

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Foreign entity's authorizing resolution or power of attorney for the Alberta partnership filing, if requested
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign entity, executed by authorized signatories; notarization by a locally competent notary where required by the recipient
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille where available and accepted; otherwise consular legalization

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Identity and address evidence for individual general and limited partners and ultimate controllers
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Government identity authority and regulated financial institution or other accepted address-document issuer in the relevant country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization and apostille or consular legalization only where required by the receiving registry agent, bank, or counterparty

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Before onboarding and periodically thereafter, identify and risk-assess domestic and foreign politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates, and screen relevant persons and counterparties against applicable Canadian sanctions and terrorist lists, UN Security Council sanctions, and OFAC lists where relevant to the transaction or payment rails. OFAC screening is not a general Canadian statutory requirement. Apply enhanced due diligence, source-of-funds and source-of-wealth review, beneficial-ownership tracing, and documented escalation where risk indicators arise. Reporting entities must follow the PCMLTFA and regulations applicable to their own regulated activities.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Alberta Corporate Registry services, accessed through an authorized Alberta registry agent; Alberta does not provide a single public-facing self-service portal that replaces registry-agent filing for all partnership registrations.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The partnership name must satisfy Alberta naming rules and be distinguishable from existing names and trademarks to the applicable standard. English, French, or combined-language names may be used. A non-Latin-script name or transliteration should be confirmed with the registry agent before filing; a registered operating name does not confer trademark rights. The name must include the required limited-partnership designation, such as 'Limited Partnership' or 'LP'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Words implying government, Crown, or official affiliation without authorization
Words implying a regulated professional, financial, insurance, banking, or other licensed activity where the required authorization is absent
Obscene, misleading, or otherwise prohibited expressions
Restricted terms for which the applicable statute, regulation, or registry policy requires consent or approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Obtain a current Alberta NUANS name search and submit the proposed name through an authorized registry agent. Confirm the reservation period and any renewal availability at filing because reservation procedures can change. If rejected, obtain the written reason, revise the name or provide supporting evidence of consent or entitlement, and request reconsideration through the registry agent or responsible Alberta registry office. If the decision is legally reviewable and administrative reconsideration is unavailable or unsuccessful, obtain Alberta counsel promptly to assess judicial review; no general statutory merits appeal should be assumed.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: An Alberta limited partnership must provide the prescribed Alberta address information for its registered office and records or service contacts as applicable to the filing. A commercial virtual-office address may be acceptable if it is a genuine, authorized address at which required records, notices, and service can be handled. A mailbox-only address may fail registry, banking, tax, or operational due-diligence requirements. Wholesale distribution does not ordinarily require a dedicated retail or warehouse premises at formation, but actual inventory, employees, and logistics arrangements should be accurately documented.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: No reliable public statistic quantifies unannounced inspections of Alberta limited partnerships. Routine physical inspection is not identified as a standard formation step for this unlicensed wholesale activity; risk is case-specific and may arise from tax, employment, safety, customs, premises, or law-enforcement inquiries.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Alberta registry agent and applicable Alberta government filing charges
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Indicative combined market estimate; confirm the current statutory charge and agent service fee before filing.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing provider and registry-agent benchmark; name search and reservation charges may be separate.

Prevailing market benchmark; varies with partner count, governance, transfer restrictions, and cross-border tax provisions.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing per-document market benchmark; not required for documents already accepted in English or French.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Compliance screening provider or professional adviser
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Indicative commercial benchmark; screening is risk-based and is not a standalone statutory formation charge for an ordinary limited partnership.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Alberta Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, Part 3 (Limited Partnerships), ss. 51–84; principally s. 52 on registration of limited partnerships and s. 54 on contents of the declaration. The Alberta Business Corporations Act does not apply to the LP itself, but applies to a corporate general partner if one is used.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta, acting through the Registrar of Companies
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership (prescribed declaration filed under the Alberta Partnership Act, RSA 2000, c P-3, s. 52)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital and no escrow requirement for an Alberta limited partnership. Capital contributions may be in cash or property as agreed in the limited partnership agreement, and need not be fully advanced at registration unless the agreement so requires.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) that the General Partner approves and adopts the Limited Partnership Agreement in the form presented and attached as Exhibit A; (2) that all subscriptions to the Partnership listed in the contribution schedule are accepted and initial capital contributions recorded; (3) that the registered office of the Partnership is established at the address specified in the registration application, and the nominated registered agent is appointed; (4) that the general partner’s designated manager is authorized to execute the registration filing, engage the public accountant, open banking accounts, obtain any municipal licence, and handle all regulatory filings; and (5) that all actions already taken to perfect formation be ratified.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name search and limited partnership name clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; online name search through RegistryX or a delegated Alberta Registry Agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Search the proposed limited partnership name against the Alberta corporate and business registry indexes. If the name contains distinctive elements, submit a Name Request and obtain approval. The cleared name must appear in the registration declaration exactly as approved.
required_dossiers: Proposed limited partnership name
General partner legal name and Alberta address
Name search report or name approval confirmation if obtained
Authorized representative contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected or flagged as confusingly similar, file a revised Name Request with a new distinguishing element. The application may be resubmitted without penalty within the registry’s standard resubmission window.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and execution of the limited partnership registration declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership, ensure the registered office is in Alberta, designate a registered agent with an Alberta address, and list all general partners. Each general partner must execute the declaration; if a corporate general partner is formed outside Alberta, it must first be extra-provincially registered in Alberta.
required_dossiers: Completed Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership
Limited partnership agreement or draft agreement
Consent of the registered agent
Certificate of extra-provincial registration for a non-Alberta corporate general partner, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registrar queries the declaration, submit an amended declaration within the notice period correcting the defect. If the query relates to the corporate general partner, cure by completing extra-provincial registration before refiling.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing, payment of fees, and issuance of certificate of registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry, Service Alberta; online submission via RegistryX
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the executed declaration to the Alberta Corporate Registry, pay the applicable registration fee, and receive the Certificate of Registration. Verify that the certificate names the LP correctly and records the general partner exactly as appointed.
required_dossiers: Executed Application for Registration of a Limited Partnership
Name approval documentation
Payment of registration fee
Registered agent consent and contact information
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is refused or suspended, cure the identified defect and file an amended application. If the registrar maintains a refusal, the applicant may seek administrative review from the Registrar of Companies or apply for relief in the Alberta Court of King's Bench, as applicable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Canada Revenue Agency business number and tax account setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency; Business Registration Online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the Alberta limited partnership with the CRA to obtain a Business Number. Open a GST/HST account if the partnership makes taxable supplies in Canada; if cross-border wholesale distribution is intended, also register with the Canada Border Services Agency for an import/export account and obtain a customs bond if required.
required_dossiers: Alberta Certificate of Registration
Limited partnership agreement
General partner identification and address
Partnership business address and contact details
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA flags inconsistent information, correct the Business Registration Online form and contact the CRA business enquiries line. If a BN is issued with an error, request a correction through My Business Account.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate governance adoption, municipal licensing, and occupational clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Alberta Corporate Registry; municipal licensing authority where the physical office or warehouse is located; Alberta occupational health and safety authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Ensure the limited partnership agreement is executed, the general partner’s board resolutions are recorded, and the registered office remains current. If the partnership occupies premises, obtain the applicable municipal business licence, comply with the Alberta Fire Code and Occupational Health and Safety Code, complete a fire safety plan, and obtain occupancy or inspection clearance before employees or inventory are placed in the premises.
required_dossiers: Executed limited partnership agreement
Certificate of Registration
Lease, occupancy agreement, or proof of premises authorization
Municipal business licence application
Fire code compliance statement and fire safety plan
Workers’ compensation registration if employees are engaged
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If municipal inspectors issue conditions or an occupancy hold, remedy each condition by completing the required fire safety, structural, and workplace inspections and resubmit the clearance documents to the issuing authority.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — Alberta does not issue an industrial operating licence for wholesale distribution of optical frames; only a municipal business licence and general workplace safety permits may apply to premises.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial industry operating licence required; municipal Business Licence may apply if a physical office or warehouse is established in Alberta.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — wholesale warehousing and distribution of ophthalmic eyewear frames does not trigger an Environmental Impact Assessment under the Environmental Protection and Enhancement Act, RSA 2000, c E-12.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or controlled emissions are expected. Any stormwater or sanitary discharge must comply with municipal sewer bylaws. If packaging or waste is generated, the Alberta Recycling Regulation and Waste Control Regulation apply for safe storage, transport, and disposal. No on-site combustion or VOC-emitting process equipment is anticipated for this wholesale activity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The premises must comply with the Alberta Fire Code and the Occupational Health and Safety Code, including fire extinguishers, exit routes, emergency lighting, and storage-rack stability. A structural load assessment is recommended for warehouse racking. The municipality may require a fire safety inspection and occupancy certificate before the premises may be lawfully used.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) - federal authority for GST/HST, income tax, partnership information returns and Business Number (BN) issuance; portal: Business Registration Online (BRO) via https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html. Provincial counterpart: Alberta Corporate Registry (Service Alberta) at https://www.alberta.ca/business-registration for limited partnership constitutive registration under the Partnership Act (RSA 2000, c P-3). Export/customs counterpart: Canada Border Services Agency (CBSA) for B13A export declarations.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Register the Alberta Limited Partnership with the Alberta Corporate Registry (OneStop) - no minimum capital, no Canadian residency requirement for partners. Step 2: Obtain a 9-digit federal Business Number (BN) from CRA via BRO; open a GST/HST program account (RT) (compulsory once taxable supplies in Canada exceed CAD 30,000 p.a., or elect voluntarily for export zero-rating and input tax credit recovery). Step 3: Open CRA Import/Export (RW) program account for CBSA clearance records. Step 4: File Form T5013 partnership information return annually with Schedule 50 (non-resident partners). Step 5: Where the LP is a non-resident registrant with no Canadian presence, appoint an agent for service; the CRA may accept the foreign partner's tax ID as associated identifier. Step 6: Maintain partner-level T1135/T1134 foreign reporting if applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible - an Alberta LP is a fiscally transparent partnership under ITA s. 96 (not an entity subject to entity-level income tax); each partner reports its share of income; non-resident partners are taxed only on Canadian-source partnership income under Part I or Part XIII as applicable. For GST/HST, however, the LP itself is a separate 'person' (registrant) under ETA s. 123(1). Canada does not permit a check-the-box election to convert the LP to corporation; classification follows the Partnership Act and ITA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box election exists in Canada; the LP status is statutory. Available elections and mechanisms: (i) Voluntary GST/HST registration election (ETA s. 240(2)) to activate zero-ratings and input tax credits; (ii) ETA s. 156 election for closely related entities (corporate general partner and LP) to treat intra-group supplies as non-taxable; (iii) ITA s. 216(1) election for a non-resident partner to be taxed on a Canadian return only upon partnership income; (iv) Hybrid-mismatch notifications and de minimis exclusions under ITA ss. 18.2-18.4 for cross-border partnership-fiscally-transparent conflicts; (v) ETA s. 243(1) election to align fiscal year for GST/HST returns; (vi) Alberta does not offer a provincial check-the-box, and the LP is exempt from Alberta corporate income tax.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST - federal value-added tax (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) under Part IX of the Excise Tax Act; Alberta imposes no provincial retail sales tax and is not an HST province, so the effective indirect tax in CA-AB is the 5% federal GST alone.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 - the small-supplier threshold under ETA s. 148(1)(c): a person (including an LP) making taxable supplies in Canada below CAD 30,000 during the immediately preceding four calendar quarters is not required to register; once exceeded, registration is compulsory. Non-resident LPs may voluntarily register regardless of threshold to zero-rate exports and recover input tax credits. ISIC 4646 (wholesale ophthalmic eyewear frames) has no special threshold or statutory licence gate.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no real-time government fiscal clearance, no digital stamping, and no mandatory API-based invoice approval regime for B2B invoices. Electronic invoices are accepted provided they meet ETA s. 223 record-keeping and the prescribed content (seller name and BN, date, description, consideration, GST rate). CRA directs electronic records retention for six years. The Pan-Canadian e-invoicing initiative (Peppol BIS 3.0) is voluntary adoption by federal/provincial governments, not a compliance mandate. Mandatory electronic filing applies to GST/HST returns (GST/HST NETFILE or GST/TELEFILE) and to large partnerships' T5013 returns (Internet File Transfer); no invoice-level clearance or stamping is required for wholesale export transactions.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating is available under ETA s. 22(1) and Schedule VI, Part V for tangible personal property (acetate eyeglass frames): the LP must (a) deliver the goods to a common carrier or freight forwarder for export to a destination outside Canada, or (b) export the goods in accordance with the Proof of Export Regulations (SOR/91-45), which require documentary evidence of export to be obtained within the prescribed period (CRA administratively expects proof of export within 60 days after the date of supply). The buyer must be a non-resident and title must pass outside Canada; sales to Canadian brokers for later export do not qualify. Associated transport, freight, customs-brokerage, and insurance services supplied to the non-resident buyer in respect of the exported goods are also zero-rated where the underlying supply is zero-rated (ETA s. 20 and Schedule VI, Part V); business-support services (offshore logistics and marketing) supplied to non-resident optical retailers not registered for GST/HST may qualify as zero-rated export services under Schedule VI, Part VII.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: CBSA B13A Canada Export Declaration (electronic) identifying the harmonised-system code for acetate optical frames and the foreign destination
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill naming the non-resident buyer or its agent and evidencing movement from Canada
Commercial invoice issued by the Alberta LP to the foreign wholesale optical customer
Proof-of-export certificate from the freight forwarder or customs broker (delivery confirmation, terminal receipt)
Inward Remittance Certificate / bank SWIFT MT103 credit advice confirming collection of export proceeds in the LP's Canadian account
Executed supply contract, purchase order, destination address evidence, and correspondence with the foreign customer
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are priority audit targets for the CRA. The registrant must retain the complete export evidence bundle for six years (ETA s. 286). Where proof-of-export documentation is missing, late, or internally inconsistent, CRA will reassess the supply as taxable at 5%, claw back input-tax credits or refunds, and charge compound daily arrears interest (ETA s. 280(1)). Gross negligence penalties can reach 50% of the understated net tax (ETA s. 285); wilful evasion or forged export documents constitute a criminal offence under ETA s. 327(1) with fines up to CAD 200,000 and/or imprisonment for up to two years. The normal four-year reassessment period extends to ten years where misrepresentation is proven. Canada sets no statutory FX-repatriation deadline, but the 180-day benchmark applied in this dossier reflects the CRA's documentary consistency expectations; failure to repatriate export proceeds within that period, without a commercial explanation, invites sham recharacterisation under ITA s. 245 GAAR, denial of the zero-rating, and transfer-pricing penalties under ITA s. 247(3).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) — Canada's central bank with monetary authority but no exchange-control administration; OSFI (Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions) supervises the Schedule I chartered banks; FINTRAC (Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada) enforces the PCMLTFA and MSB/EFT reporting; the Minister of Finance administers the Exchange Fund Account under the Financial Administration Act; Payments Canada operates the Lynx high-value CAD settlement system and the ACSS batch retail clearing system. No Canadian authority grants FX permits or approves capital flows.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains IMF Article VIII current-account convertibility; the Canadian dollar is freely convertible on both capital and current accounts with no statutory approvals, quotas, or licensing for foreign direct investment, capital calls, profit remittances, or loan servicing. The wartime Foreign Exchange Control Act was repealed in 1952; the Bank of Canada does not require notification for LP capital subscriptions or distributions. Functional hurdles are tax-driven, not FX-driven: a non-resident LP partner is taxable in Canada under Part I on its share of Canadian-business income (via the partnership's permanent establishment), and passive flows (interest, royalties, management fees) attract Part XIII withholding subject to treaty relief (e.g., under the Canada-US Tax Treaty). Neither issue constitutes a foreign-exchange restriction. Administrative friction arises through bank KYC, corporate substance expectations, and CRS/FATCA self-certification obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No surrender or conversion regime exists. Canada does not require export proceeds to be repatriated, converted, or liquidated within any statutory timeline, and there is no mandatory conversion ratio. The LP may hold export receivables in USD/EUR indefinitely in a foreign-currency account at a Schedule I bank, or convert them at market rate. FINTRAC only imposes record-keeping and cross-border EFT reporting (threshold CAD 10,000) plus standard sanctions screening, which the bank executes on its own account.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 days following each anniversary date of limited partnership registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fee CAD 100 per filing period; continuing default for two consecutive years may result in administrative cancellation or strike-off of the limited partnership registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: T5013 Partnership Information Return and Partner Schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before March 31 following a December 31 fiscal year-end; if the fiscal year-end differs, on or before the day that is five months after the fiscal year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of CAD 25 per day up to CAD 2,500 per T5013 return; partner income allocations may be reassessed.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year fiscal period, no later than March 31 of the following year; generally within three months of fiscal period year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file remittance triggers 5% late-filing penalty plus 1% per month for up to 12 months, plus statutory interest on unpaid amounts.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No automatic statutory audit under the Alberta Partnership Act; an independent audit becomes compulsory if required by the partnership agreement, a court order, a lender covenant, or if the limited partnership is a reporting issuer under Canadian securities law; otherwise, an audit is generally expected only when annual revenue or assets exceed C$10 million as an institutional covenant threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP per CPA Canada Handbook; private limited partnerships may adopt Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE); public accountable enterprises must apply IFRS.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each year, as part of the Alberta Limited Partnership Annual Return, the general partner must confirm the complete list of general and limited partners and disclose any transfers or assignments of partnership interests; any changes must also be filed via a Declaration of Change within 60 days. This annual update serves as the beneficial-ownership confirmation for anti-money-laundering compliance and Alberta corporate registry transparency.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Assignments and Transfers of Limited Partnership Interests
Minute Book maintained by the General Partner for resolutions and unanimous partner agreements

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: CAD 150 - CAD 450 (approx. USD 115 - 345) per year for registered office services in Alberta
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: CAD 3,500 - CAD 12,000 (approx. USD 2,700 - 9,200) for financial statement preparation and independent audit, if triggered; compilation-only services range lower

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 23% combined (15% federal + 8% Alberta general corporate rate); the Alberta Limited Partnership is fiscally transparent, so income tax is borne by each partner on the allocated share. A Canadian-controlled private corporation (CCPC) partner may apply the reduced 11% combined rate (9% federal + 2% Alberta) on up to CAD 500,000 of qualified active business income flowing through the LP.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Alberta small business deduction at 2% provincial (aligned with federal 9% SBD) for CCPC partners on their allocated active business income up to CAD 500,000; federal SR&ED investment tax credits (refundable 35% for CCPCs up to the expenditure limit); Alberta Innovation Employment Grant; no Alberta capital tax. The LP itself is not entitled to tax holidays; however, non-resident corporate partners carrying on business through the LP face a 25% Part I branch tax under s.219 of the Income Tax Act (Canada), reduced to 5% under the Canada-US Treaty and to 10-15% under most other Canadian DTAs.
